text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- A former Russian citizen has accused one of Russia's biggest banks of embezzling $7,2 million.

- The secretary of Russia's Security Council Ivan Rybkin has dismissed rumours that the State Duma lower house of parliament is about to be dissolved but does not rule out the possibility of early parliamentary polls if the Duma continues to resist reforms.
- U.S. officials and Russian bankers say the issue of new $50 bills will not create any problems in the country.
- The Far Eastern Primorye region's governor Yevgeny Nazdratenko has started an anti-Moscow campaign, apparently in preparation for a possible early election.
- First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais urged the government to speed up the process of converting all budget monetary operations from commercial banks to the state treasury.
- Russia's gold market will be liberalised no earlier than a year from now.
SEVODNYA
- The State Duma turned down the government's programme of social reforms.
- The likely re-election of Yevgeny Nazdratenko with his strong anti-federal ambitions would be a disaster for Moscow.
- President Yeltsin's decree on pensions which guarantees payment of just 80 percent of the living wage to the elderly shocked State Duma deputies.
- Russia will remain a member of the international space programme Alpha after Russian banks agreed to sponsor construction of the service module.
- Russian investors lost $52 million in a battle for Kazakh grain. Despite various high-level agreements, economic links are not easily restored.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- The activities of a team of young reformers in the government have a very high profile but bring few results.
- Russia needs a carefully thought-out strategy for local budgets.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA
- The economic crisis in Primorye is turning into a serious political conflict as people there begin to talk about creating a separate Maritime Republic.
PRAVDA-5
- The government has prepared a dangerous package of social bills.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- The Kremlin is preparing a new campaign against regional leaders.
-- Svetlana Kovaleva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
